lead: the ground was a field with a slope on it and a padlock nobody had a key to. seventeen families arrange their saturdays around what you put there, and nobody ever put any of it to you.
sun: everything on that site went up because you decided it should, and the deciding is the part kept out of sight: which subs get waived, whose kit came off your own account, which boy is being carried this season. the families are looking at a club. what carries it is one person's arrangement, held out of view on purpose, since a boy whose subs are waived cannot be allowed to learn it.
moon: you have never had a requirement in there — no preference about fixtures, nothing anybody has to satisfy — so the space keeps taking deposits. somebody decided you were the one who talks to the league. somebody else decided you were the one to ring when a father is picked up on a friday night. neither decision was ever said to you. both are now what the club does.
pull: you cannot decline a job that was never offered, and you cannot show the size of the pile, because keeping the inside out of view is what the thing was built to do.
tension: the load could be halved in one evening if the seventeen of them saw it on one sheet. the sheet cannot exist: half its lines have a family's name against them and the other half a boy's, and producing it would put a dozen households' business on one page. so nothing ever comes off, and each season adds an item, arriving as thanks. what they see is somebody who never minds, and nothing on view says otherwise.
cost: a boy turns up on a wednesday with no kit and nobody bringing him, and by saturday he is playing, with no form to complete and nobody who had to be persuaded. every line of that rests on one person, who is also the only one who could count them. a year you cannot do it reaches seventeen households in the same fortnight, as the thing having gone.

lead: people ring you at night on purpose, and say the second-worst thing, and you take the worst one off the sound of the sentence. then you put the phone down and go and do something, where nobody is looking.
sun: being reachable at that hour was built, not inherited: the number unchanged since you were twenty-four, work chosen because it can absorb a bad morning, a room where a call can be taken without waking the house. and what happens next goes on out of sight — the surgery rung at nine, the brother headed off, a week rearranged so that thursday is survivable for somebody who does not know thursday was ever in question.
moon: what gets heard sits under the sentence rather than in it: that this is the fourth night, that the leaving already happened in the summer, that a question about the ferry is a question about going back at all. you answer the sentence they said. the other one goes in, and gets worked on, and no version of it is ever quoted back to them.
pull: they remember being listened to. what they cannot remember is the week that got easier afterwards, because the part that did it was done underneath, by one person, on no rota.
tension: the thanks are always for the conversation. nobody using that number has been given a fact about how it runs — no total, no other names, no night that was the wrong night to ring — so what gets thanked is an hour of attention, and the week that was quietly rebuilt afterwards never comes up at all. raising it means describing the other calls, which is the one move the arrangement was designed to make impossible.
cost: nothing comes back down the line that anybody has to manage: no advice, no question they cannot answer, no difference in how they are met at a table a fortnight later. one number, one person behind it, and no other line written down anywhere, so a season you cannot pick up reaches all of them in the same week, with nobody warned, including you.

lead: twice a day for nineteen years, and the interval between the two is the only shape your life has. two families draw a wage off that interval, and neither of them has ever seen it slip.
sun: the cover here is a plural. the paperwork carries a name that sounds like a firm, the invoices say the yard rather than a person, and the vet gets greeted as though somebody were in an office somewhere doing the books. that was arranged deliberately, and it is what lets two households take on a mortgage against what is actually one person's back and one person's willingness to get up.
moon: animals do not accept a poor week. the hour is set by them rather than by anybody who can be reasoned with, and no part of it can be done at half pace, no month of going carefully while something mends. what the two families call the routine is a load that arrives on the hour whether or not you can lift it.
pull: the pace and the one support are the same object, and that object never slows and never leans. nothing in nineteen years has rehearsed anybody for the morning it fails to arrive.
tension: somebody covers a fortnight in the autumn and reports back that it was fine, which is honest and is the wrong lesson, because a fortnight is the only unit anybody can be shown. what cannot be shown is the arithmetic of never having stopped — and putting that on a table means telling two households what their mortgages are attached to, and telling a bank the identical thing that afternoon. so the fortnight stands as the record.
cost: a herd came through a bad winter with nobody on that payroll losing a day's pay or hearing how close it had been. one pair of hands does it, presented as several, and the arrangement shows nobody a place to take weight off. the hands go on a tuesday and two households and a yard full of animals learn the same fact before ten in the morning.

lead: bring them here is something you have said in plain words, more than once, to people who took it up the same month. what a day of it takes has never been put into words anywhere at all.
sun: the offer is genuine and the accounting behind it is sealed. nobody who has brought a person to your door has been shown the evening afterwards, or the leave booked to make the day possible, or the conversation at home that had to happen first. an offer with a price showing is not an offer anybody in trouble can take up, so hiding the price is part of making the room.
moon: room gets made out loud, on a date, in the hearing of the person it is for — which is the half that works. they can put a hand up without a case to argue, because the terms were said in a full sentence. what the sentence does not carry is any figure. so it goes out at a flat rate, and it gets taken up at a flat rate.
pull: the room only works if it looks free. making it look free is the other half of the work, and nobody who has used the room has been let near that half.
tension: nobody can size a request, because nothing about the underside has been published. a genuine emergency and an ordinary convenience arrive in the same words and get the same afternoon, and anybody who would have rationed themselves is rationing against nothing. the autumn you had something of your own to carry, the requests came in at exactly the rate they always come in, because no signal was available that anybody could have read.
cost: somebody's mother gets left at your kitchen table at nine and collected at six, with no form, no fee, and nothing said about whether it suited. one person is the capacity, presented as a house with room in it, and nobody can see a place to help. the week it cannot happen, it does not happen, and the people it was holding up find out on the morning.
